# Offer of employment — Junior Consultant Sales (FAIS) - Riviersonderend

## 1. Job Offer: Junior Consultant Sales (FAIS) - Riviersonderend

Dear {{employee.full_name}},

We are happy to offer you the position of Junior Consultant Sales (FAIS) - Riviersonderend at Absa Group. This is a permanent position starting on 1 December 2026. Your place of work will be Riviersonderend, head office.

## 2. Your Duties

You will make self-initiated contact with customers to meet sales targets. You will work with your team, share knowledge, and give helpful feedback. You will follow all compliance and risk rules and quality standards. You will give customers excellent service.

## 3. Hours and Pay

You will work 40 hours a week, 8 hours a day, Monday to Friday, from 08:00 to 17:00. You get a 60-minute meal break after no more than five hours of work. Your basic salary is R18,000.00 per month. You will be paid on the 25th of each month by EFT. PAYE and UIF of 1% will be deducted from your pay.

## 4. Probation

Your first 3 months will be a probation period. During this time, we will check how you are doing in the job and support you with guidance and training where needed.

## 5. Before You Start

Please send your ID and qualifications to hr@example.co.za. This offer is open until 30 November 2026.

## 6. Acceptance

Please sign and date this letter by {{date_signed}} to accept this offer.

contract.markdown:
# Contract of employment — Junior Consultant Sales (FAIS) - Riviersonderend

## 1. Parties

This contract of employment is entered into between Absa Group, of 1 Main Road, Riviersonderend (the Employer), and {{employee.full_name}}, identity number {{employee.id_number}}, of {{employee.address}} (the Employee).

## 2. Position and duties

The Employer appoints the Employee as Junior Consultant Sales (FAIS) - Riviersonderend. The Employee's duties include: Sales Target : Proactively make self-initiated contact with customers in order to deliver against the required sales targets; Collaboration : Constantly seek to improve ways of working by challenging the status quo and supporting an empowering climate within the team, sharing knowledge, experience, best practice and providing constructive feedback as required.; Compliance and Risk Management: Fulfil all activities in adherence to relevant control and compliance requirements, and quality standards; Customer Experience: To provide service excellence and achieve customer satisfaction. The Employer may reasonably require the Employee to perform other duties consistent with the position.

## 3. Commencement

Employment commences on 1 December 2026 on a permanent basis.

## 4. Probation

The first 3 month(s) of employment are a probationary period during which the Employer will assess the Employee's performance against the requirements of the position and give reasonable evaluation, instruction, training, guidance or counselling where needed. Confirmation, extension or termination at the end of probation will follow a fair procedure.

## 5. Place of work

The Employee's place of work is Riviersonderend, head office.

## 6. Hours of work

The Employee's ordinary hours of work are 40 hours per week, 8 hours per day over 5 days per week (Mon–Fri 08:00–17:00). A meal interval of 60 minutes is taken after no more than five hours of continuous work. The Employee is entitled to a daily rest period of at least 12 consecutive hours and a weekly rest period of at least 36 consecutive hours.

## 7. Remuneration

The Employee will be paid R18,000.00 per month (basic salary), equivalent to R103.85 per ordinary hour, payable monthly on the 25th by EFT. No other cash payments are payable. No payments in kind are made.

## 8. Overtime

Overtime is worked only by agreement and may not exceed ten hours in any week. Overtime is paid at 1.5 times the Employee's ordinary hourly wage, or, by agreement, compensated with paid time off. Work on a Sunday is paid at double the ordinary wage (or one and a half times if the Employee ordinarily works on Sundays), and work on a public holiday at double the ordinary wage.

## 9. Deductions

The following deductions will be made from the Employee's remuneration: PAYE; UIF 1%. No other deduction will be made without the Employee's written agreement in respect of a specific debt, or as required by law, a court order or an arbitration award.

## 10. Leave

The Employee is entitled to 15 working days of paid annual leave per annual leave cycle of 12 months, to be taken at a time agreed with the Employer and not later than six months after the end of the cycle. Sick leave: 30 days' paid sick leave in every 36-month cycle (during the first six months, one day for every 26 days worked); a medical certificate may be required for absences of more than two consecutive days or on more than two occasions in eight weeks. Maternity leave: at least 4 consecutive months. Parental leave: 10 consecutive days. Adoption and commissioning parental leave as provided in the Act. Family responsibility leave: 3 days' paid leave per year once employed for longer than four months and for at least four days a week.

## 11. Termination and notice

Either party may terminate this contract on written notice of one week if the employee has been employed for six months or less; two weeks if employed for more than six months but not more than one year; four weeks if employed for more than one year. Notice may not be given during any period of leave. Nothing in this clause prevents the Employer from terminating employment summarily for a fair reason following a fair procedure, or the parties from agreeing to waive notice.

## 12. Bargaining council or sectoral determination

No bargaining council agreement or sectoral determination applies to the Employer's business.

## 13. Confidentiality

The Employee will not, during or after employment, disclose or use any confidential information of the Employer, its clients or suppliers, except as required to perform the Employee's duties or by law.

## 14. Other documents

No other documents form part of this contract.

## 15. General

This contract records the whole agreement between the parties on its subject; any amendment must be in writing and signed by both parties. Where any term is less favourable to the Employee than the Basic Conditions of Employment Act or an applicable sectoral determination or collective agreement, the more favourable provision applies. The Employer will keep these particulars for three years after termination and will explain them to the Employee on request.

## 16. Signatures

Signed at ____________ on {{date_signed}}.

For the Employer: {{employer.signatory}}  ____________________

The Employee: {{employee.full_name}}  ____________________

plain_language.explanation: This clause names who is making the agreement: Absa Group as the employer, based at 1 Main Road, Riviersonderend, and you as the employee. It records your ID number and address as part of the contract.

You are being hired as a Junior Consultant Sales (FAIS) for Riviersonderend. Your main duties are making sales contact with customers, working well with your team, following compliance rules, and giving good customer service. Your employer can also ask you to do other reasonable tasks that fit this role.
Your job starts on 1 December 2026. This is a permanent job, not a fixed-term or temporary one.

Your first 3 months are a trial period where your employer checks your performance. During this time, you will get fair evaluation, training, and guidance. Any decision to confirm, extend, or end your job after probation must follow a fair process.
You will work at the Riviersonderend head office. This is the fixed location for your job.

You work 40 hours a week, 8 hours a day, over 5 days, Monday to Friday from 08:00 to 17:00. You get a 60-minute meal break if you work more than five hours straight. You are also entitled to at least 12 hours of rest between workdays and at least 36 hours of rest each week.
Your basic salary is R18,000.00 per month, which works out to R103.85 per hour. You are paid monthly on the 25th by EFT. You will not receive any other cash payments or payments in kind.

You can only work overtime if you agree to it, and it cannot be more than 10 hours a week. Overtime pay is 1.5 times your normal hourly rate, or you can agree to take paid time off instead. If you work on a Sunday, you get double pay (or 1.5 times if you normally work Sundays), and public holiday work is paid at double your normal wage.
Your employer will deduct PAYE (income tax) and 1% for UIF from your pay. No other deductions will be made unless you agree in writing, or the law, a court, or an arbitration order requires it.

You get 15 working days of paid annual leave each year, to be taken at a time agreed with your employer, and used within six months after the leave year ends. You get 30 days of paid sick leave every 3 years, though in your first six months you earn 1 day for every 26 days worked; your employer can ask for a medical certificate if you're off more than two days in a row or more than twice in eight weeks. You can take at least 4 months of maternity leave and 10 consecutive days of parental leave, plus leave if you adopt a child as set out in the law. After four months of employment, working at least four days a week, you get 3 days of paid family responsibility leave each year.

Either you or your employer can end the contract with written notice: one week if you've worked six months or less, two weeks if you've worked more than six months but up to a year, and four weeks if you've worked more than a year. Notice cannot be given while you are on leave. Your employer can still dismiss you immediately for a serious reason if a fair process is followed, and both sides can agree to skip the notice period.
No bargaining council agreement or sectoral determination applies to your employer's business. This means industry-specific wage or condition rules from a council or determination do not apply here.

You must not share or use confidential information belonging to your employer, its clients, or suppliers, whether you are still employed or have left. You can use or share this information only if it's needed to do your job or required by law.
No other documents are part of this contract besides what is written here.

This contract contains the full agreement between you and your employer, and any changes must be written and signed by both of you. If any part of this contract is worse for you than the Basic Conditions of Employment Act or any relevant sectoral determination or collective agreement, the better rule for you will apply. Your employer will keep your employment records for three years after you leave and will explain them to you if you ask.
This is the signature section. The employer's signatory signs for Absa Group, and you, {{employee.full_name}}, sign to confirm you accept the contract, both on the date shown as {{date_signed}}.
